num_customers: int; number of customers N, excluding the depot; unit: count; must be a non-negative integer; N=0 is allowed. Scalar, no array axis. Nodes are numbered 0..N, where 0 is the depot and customers are mathematically numbered 1..N; every customer-only input array maps 0-based position p to customer i=p+1, with no depot placeholder entry added.
planning_period: int; number of days T in the planning period; unit: days; must be a positive integer; T=1 is allowed. Scalar, no array axis. Days use 0-based numbering t=0..T-1.
num_vehicles: int; number of vehicles K available each day; unit: vehicles; must be a positive integer. Scalar, no array axis. Mathematical vehicle numbering is k=1..K; the output vehicle axis uses 0-based position h=0..K-1, corresponding to k=h+1. All vehicles have the same capacity vehicle_capacity every day.
vehicle_capacity: float (JSON number; integer notation allowed); the common capacity Q of all vehicles; must be a strictly positive finite real. Scalar, no array axis. The unit is a uniform capacity unit, the same as demands; the specific physical unit is unspecified.
distance_matrix: list[list[float]] (elements are JSON numbers; integer notation allowed); shape (N+1)×(N+1), axes in order: origin node i × destination node j; distance_matrix[i][j] is exactly d_ij, and both axes use node numbers 0..N directly, including the depot. The unit is a uniform distance unit; the specific unit is unspecified. Elements must be non-negative finite reals representing Euclidean distances; the diagonal is 0, and the matrix is symmetric and satisfies the triangle inequality of Euclidean distances. The given values are used directly in the total travel distance objective, without additional rounding, scaling or recomputation. When N=0 it is [[0]].
demands: list[float] (elements are JSON numbers; integer notation allowed); length N; the only axis is the customer 0-based position p; demands[p] is the demand q_i of customer i=p+1, excluding the depot. Each entry must be a strictly positive finite real, in the same unit as vehicle_capacity. Every visit to the customer counts the full q_i; it is not apportioned by the number of visits. q_i greater than Q is not an input-domain violation, but it leads to infeasibility. When N=0 it is [].
candidate_schedules: list[list[int]]; outer length N; the outer axis is the customer 0-based position p, corresponding to customer i=p+1; the inner axis is the local position r among that customer's candidate schedules. The value of candidate_schedules[p][r] is the global schedule number s in schedule_vectors. Let M=len(schedule_vectors); then s must be an integer in 0..M-1; each customer's inner list must be non-empty, and the same schedule number must not repeat within one customer's list. Different customers may reference the same schedule number. The inner input order is preserved, and row p of output x is aligned by the same local position r. When N=0 it is [].
schedule_vectors: list[list[int]]; shape M×T, where M is determined by the number of rows of this field; there is no separate num_schedules field. Axes in order: global schedule number s=0..M-1 × day t=0..T-1; schedule_vectors[s][t] is a_st and must be the integer 0 or 1; booleans are not accepted. 1 means the customer must be served on that day if this schedule is selected; 0 means it must not be served on that day; every row must contain at least one 1. The schedule table registers all schedules referenced by candidate_schedules, and every row is referenced by at least one customer, so that the set of schedule numbers is exactly the union of all customers' candidate sets. Different schedule numbers may have identical service-day vectors and are not merged. When N=0 it is []; when N>0, M>=1.
